sampler.schedule: 20-step cosine DDPM; native CPU float32 coefficients
sampler.evaluation_description: Evaluation uses DPPO's "deterministic" mode, which retains the DDPM's own noise sqrt(beta_tilde_t) at every step except the noiseless last step; the numerical lower bound never binds, since the minimum sqrt(beta_tilde_t) for t >= 1 is approximately 0.076.
sampler.training_description: Training raises the noise standard deviation to at least 0.1, which binds only at the final two denoising steps. At the final step it adds nominal N(0, 0.1^2) noise to each action coordinate, so training returns sit below evaluation returns.
sampler.noise_truncation_note: DPPO retains its original clipping of standard-normal draws at +/-3; the other two methods use +/-100. The Gaussian description is before this clipping.
sampler.reset_seeding_note: The wrapper's seed() updates NumPy's global generator, while reset() calls the inner environment without passing a seed; the MuJoCo reset generator is not seeded by this wrapper.

captions.eval: One seed per method (seed 0), 80 episodes per point. The x-axis is training environment steps used before the rollout. The shared starting mean pools 240 original episodes; its episode standard error is unavailable because episode dispersion was not saved. No seed bands are shown. Evaluation uses DPPO's "deterministic" mode, which retains the DDPM's own noise sqrt(beta_tilde_t) at every step except the noiseless last step; the numerical lower bound never binds, since the minimum sqrt(beta_tilde_t) for t >= 1 is approximately 0.076. DPPO's seed-to-seed sd at the final evaluation is about 108 (3 seeds), so the difference between two single-seed curves has sd of about 150.
captions.train: One seed per method (seed 0), 80 episodes per point. The x-axis is training environment steps used before the rollout. The shared starting mean pools 240 original episodes; its episode standard error is unavailable because episode dispersion was not saved. No seed bands are shown. No smoothing. Training raises the noise standard deviation to at least 0.1, which binds only at the final two denoising steps. At the final step it adds nominal N(0, 0.1^2) noise to each action coordinate, so training returns sit below evaluation returns. DPPO retains its original +/-3-sigma truncation of the nominal Gaussian noise.
